tasks.title: Build ngv2/confidence_signals.py: live compute_confidence signal producer (scan + semantic proofs + confirmed live-detonation verdict)
acceptance_criteria: ngv2/confidence_signals.py exists with EXACTLY the content given in the brief's Deliverables block and is importable as ngv2.confidence_signals.
build_confidence_signals(finding, *, semantic_signals=None, live_report=None) -> list[dict] is exposed at module scope.
A finding carrying 'id' or 'category' contributes exactly one {'tool':'pattern_scanner','kind':'pattern','result':'match'} signal; an empty/None or id-less finding contributes none.
Provided P3.1 semantic_signals (taint_flow/formal_path proof dicts) are merged through verbatim, with non-dict items skipped.

A live_report (dict or object) whose 'verdict' or 'semantic_verdict' equals 'confirmed' (case-insensitive, whitespace-stripped) contributes {'tool':'poc_runner','kind':'live_poc','result':'proof'}; any non-confirmed/missing verdict contributes nothing.
Assembled order is pattern match, then semantic signals, then live_poc; the function is pure/deterministic with no I/O, clock, randomness, or subprocess.
No other module is modified (grounding_confidence_gate, session_gate, semantic_signals, poc_runner_live, _e2e_run/* are untouched).

spec.objective: Create a single new orchestration module ngv2/confidence_signals.py that assembles the live compute_confidence signal list from the real regex scan finding (a 'pattern' match), the P3.1 structural semantic signals (taint_flow/formal_path proofs merged through verbatim), and a REAL live-detonation report (only a 'confirmed' verdict yields a 'live_poc' structural proof) -- replacing the hand-faked signals=[...] literal in _e2e_run/drive_one.py with DERIVED values, while a non-confirmed verdict can never manufacture confidence.
functional_requirements: Expose build_confidence_signals(finding: dict, *, semantic_signals: list | None = None, live_report=None) -> list[dict] in ngv2/confidence_signals.py, importable as ngv2.confidence_signals.
Helper _scan_match_signal(finding) returns {'tool':'pattern_scanner','kind':'pattern','result':'match'} when finding is truthy and carries an 'id' or 'category'; otherwise returns None.
The provided semantic_signals list is appended verbatim in order, skipping any non-dict element; a None/empty semantic_signals adds nothing.

Helper _live_poc_signal(live_report) reads 'verdict' then 'semantic_verdict' from a dict (via .get) or object (via getattr) and returns {'tool':'poc_runner','kind':'live_poc','result':'proof'} only when that value str-stripped-lowercased equals 'confirmed'.
A non-confirmed verdict (unconfirmed/inconclusive/refuted) or a missing/None live_report yields no live_poc signal.

build_confidence_signals composes results in order [pattern match, semantic signals..., live_poc] and remains pure/deterministic and total over malformed input (no I/O, clock, randomness, subprocess, network, or LLM).
spec.interfaces: build_confidence_signals(finding: dict, *, semantic_signals: list[dict] | None = None, live_report: dict | object | None = None) -> list[dict]; module-private helpers _scan_match_signal(finding) -> dict|None and _live_poc_signal(live_report) -> dict|None. Output dicts are {'tool','kind','result'} consumed by ngv2.grounding_confidence_gate.compute_confidence (kind in {taint_flow,formal_path,live_poc} with result=='proof' -> CONFIRMED; exactly one 'match' result -> MEDIUM).
edge_cases: finding is {} or None -> no pattern signal.
finding has only 'category' (no 'id') -> still yields a pattern match.
semantic_signals is None -> no semantic entries; semantic_signals contains a non-dict (e.g. None or str) -> that element is skipped.
live_report verdict 'CONFIRMED' / ' confirmed ' (mixed case / padded) -> still yields a live_poc proof.
live_report uses 'semantic_verdict' instead of 'verdict' -> read correctly.
live_report is an object exposing .verdict / .semantic_verdict attributes rather than a dict.
live_report verdict is 'unconfirmed' / 'inconclusive' / 'refuted' / None, or live_report is None -> no live_poc proof.
non_goals: Do NOT modify ngv2/grounding_confidence_gate.py, ngv2/session_gate.py, ngv2/semantic_signals.py, ngv2/poc_runner_live.py, or _e2e_run/* (the drive_one.py wiring is out of scope).
Do NOT call the network, a subprocess, a clock, or an LLM; no randomness; do NOT detonate anything -- the verdict is read from the already-computed report dict.
spec.implementation_notes:
Emit ngv2/confidence_signals.py EXACTLY as given in the brief's Deliverables block (verbatim, including the module docstring, `from __future__ import annotations`, typing imports, both private helpers, and the public build_confidence_signals). Do not add or rename functions, change ordering, or alter the returned dict shapes.

# CREDENTIAL-NAMING CONSTRAINT (the AST security gate FAILS the build if a variable whose name contains (case-insensitive) "password", "secret", or "key" is assigned a string literal -- it reads as a hardcoded credential even though this is an external clean-room target with no real secret). NEVER bind a string literal to such a variable. Use a neutral name instead (field_name, check_id, label, name, ident, column) or iterate a collection literal / build the mapping from a list of tuples. This applies to dict keys held in a temp var, field labels, and constant identifiers.

# STDLIB-ONLY CONSTRAINT (the verification environment installs NO third-party packages, so importing one fails collection -> the whole build is rolled back and the leaf is parked). Import ONLY the Python standard library. Import NO third-party package: NO pydantic, NO pydantic_settings, NO attrs, NO pyyaml, NO numpy, NO requests, etc. For data models / config use stdlib dataclasses (dataclasses.dataclass), enum.Enum, typing, and plain dict / json instead of pydantic BaseModel / BaseSettings. If the spec mentions pydantic-style validation, re-express it with stdlib dataclasses + manual checks.

# DETERMINISM CONSTRAINT (the AST nondeterminism gate FAILS the build if it sees a wall-clock or nondeterministic source). Do NOT call datetime.now / datetime.utcnow, time.time / time.monotonic, unseeded random, uuid, os.urandom, or secrets to obtain a timestamp / id / randomness. Instead accept any timestamp, seed, or clock as an EXPLICIT parameter with a deterministic default (the oracle injects it, e.g. via now_fn / make_scripted_clock), so the same inputs always produce the same output.

test_spec.test_data_requirements: Findings: {'id':'x'}, {'category':'path-traversal'}, {}, None. Semantic signal dicts shaped {'tool':...,'kind':'taint_flow','result':'proof'} plus a non-dict element. Live reports as dicts with verdict in {'confirmed','CONFIRMED',' confirmed ','unconfirmed','inconclusive','refuted',None} and a variant using 'semantic_verdict', plus an object exposing .verdict.

token_budget_ratio.note: Implementation is a verbatim emission of a small pure module; the bulk of effort is the behavioral oracle proving the scan/semantic/live-verdict assembly and the marker-spoofing guard.

tasks.title: Author committed oracle tests/test_confidence_signals_wired.py wiring build_confidence_signals into compute_confidence
acceptance_criteria: tests/test_confidence_signals_wired.py exists and is the file named in the verification_command.
Oracle asserts scan-only finding -> build_confidence_signals returns exactly one 'pattern' match -> ngv2.grounding_confidence_gate.compute_confidence yields MEDIUM.
Oracle asserts a 'confirmed' live_report -> a 'live_poc' proof is present -> compute_confidence yields CONFIRMED.
Oracle asserts unconfirmed/inconclusive/refuted/None live_report -> no 'live_poc' proof in the output.
Oracle asserts full assembly (scan + taint_flow semantic + confirmed live_poc) carries all three kinds -> compute_confidence yields CONFIRMED.
The suite passes via the verification_command and fails against the module's declared mutant (non-vacuous).

spec.objective: Commit the behavioral oracle that pins build_confidence_signals to its consumer ngv2.grounding_confidence_gate.compute_confidence, proving the scan->MEDIUM, confirmed-detonation->CONFIRMED, non-confirmed->no-proof, and full-assembly->CONFIRMED semantics, and that a print-only marker cannot manufacture confidence.
functional_requirements: Assert: a scan finding (with 'id' or 'category') and no semantic/live input -> build returns exactly one 'pattern' match signal -> compute_confidence(...) == MEDIUM.
Assert: a live_report with verdict 'confirmed' -> output contains a {'kind':'live_poc','result':'proof'} signal -> compute_confidence(...) == CONFIRMED.
Assert: live_report verdict in {'unconfirmed','inconclusive','refuted'} or live_report None -> output contains NO 'live_poc' proof.
Assert: full assembly (scan finding + a taint_flow semantic proof + confirmed live_report) -> output carries kinds {'pattern','taint_flow','live_poc'} -> compute_confidence(...) == CONFIRMED.
spec.interfaces: Imports ngv2.confidence_signals.build_confidence_signals and ngv2.grounding_confidence_gate.compute_confidence; constructs finding dicts, semantic signal dicts ({'tool','kind':'taint_flow','result':'proof'}), and live_report dicts; reads the CONFIRMED/MEDIUM verdict labels from grounding_confidence_gate's public surface rather than hard-coding raw strings where an enum/constant exists.
edge_cases: live_report supplied via 'semantic_verdict' field as well as 'verdict'.
semantic_signals list containing a non-dict element is tolerated and excluded.
Empty/id-less finding contributes no pattern match (so scan-only with {} does not reach MEDIUM via a phantom signal).
non_goals: Do NOT modify ngv2/confidence_signals.py or any other module under test; this task only adds the test file.
Do NOT exercise network/subprocess/clock/LLM/randomness or perform real detonation; all live verdicts are passed as in-memory report dicts.
spec.implementation_notes: Place the file at tests/test_confidence_signals_wired.py so it matches the verification_command. Drive compute_confidence with the assembled signal lists to verify the gate's MEDIUM (exactly one 'match') and CONFIRMED (structural proof kind in {taint_flow,formal_path,live_poc} with result=='proof') classifications. Keep assertions tight enough that mutating _live_poc_signal's 'confirmed' guard, the scan id-check, or the assembly order causes a failure (non-vacuity against the declared mutant).

test_spec.test_data_requirements: Finding dicts {'id':'x'} and {'category':'path-traversal'}; a taint_flow semantic proof dict {'tool':'semantic','kind':'taint_flow','result':'proof'}; live_report dicts spanning verdict in {'confirmed','CONFIRMED',' confirmed ','unconfirmed','inconclusive','refuted',None} including one using 'semantic_verdict'. Expected labels read from ngv2.grounding_confidence_gate (MEDIUM, CONFIRMED).
